meaning:
δῶμα, -τος, τό
(δέμω, to build), [in LXX for גָּג ;]
chiefly in poets and late (not Attic) prose;
1. a house, hall.
2. In LXX (and Hom., Od., x, 554; cf. MGr., terrace), house-top: ἐπὶ τ. δῶμα, Luk.5:19, Act.10:9; ἐπὶ τ. δώματος, -άτων, Mat.10:27 24:17, Mrk.13:15, Luk.12:3 17:31.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: What I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear whispered in the ear, proclaim on the housetops.
and let him who is on the housetop not go down, nor enter in, to take anything out of his house.
Not finding a way to bring him in because of the multitude, they went up to the housetop, and let him down through the tiles with his cot into the middle…
Now on the next day as they were on their journey, and got close to the city, Peter went up on the housetop to pray at about noon.
